title: Equality at the health centre
body: At a busy government health centre, patients wait in a single queue for medicines. When a young man tries to jump the queue, the others protest and he is sent back to his place; everyone feels relieved that each person gets an equal chance. Next to the main queue there is a separate counter for elderly patients and persons with disabilities, and no one objects to it. Raju, a day labourer who carries bricks at a construction site, waits patiently in the queue. When his turn comes, he learns that the doctor has prescribed medicines that are not free, and he cannot afford them. His daughter has also been kept at home to look after her younger brother while he works. Some patients say that the queue was fair to everyone; others say that a fair queue alone does not make the system fair.
